sections.overview: Rabb’s Fringe-limbed Treefrog is known from the mountains around El Valle de Antón in central Panama.
sections.identification: It is a large treefrog with extensive webbing on the hands and feet, enabling short glides.
sections.habitat: It inhabits premontane forest around El Valle de Antón, at roughly 900–1150 m elevation.
sections.diet: The species account provides no specific prey list.
sections.behavior: Males call from tree holes and guard the eggs and tadpoles.
sections.reproduction: Females lay clutches of about 60–200 eggs above water inside tree holes, and males attend the eggs and tadpoles.
sections.ecology: A 2025 acoustic survey found no evidence of the frog, while the IUCN assessment records continuing habitat decline and possible disease impacts.
sections.conservation: The IUCN lists it as Critically Endangered (Possibly Extinct); the last known captive individual died in 2016.
